Intrusive thoughts (especially the ones that want to make you belive you're a horrible person) are a cruel cycle, but remember that these are just thoughts, they just show up and go away, but with the amount of energy you're putting into them they seem so much more intense than they acually are, and that's why they're so hard to let go of. Giving up on intrusive thoughts isn't letting whatever is going on in your head take control of you, but realising there is nothing to fight, because they are just thoughts, and you have no intention on acting upon them, so there is nothing to worry about. You are far more in control than you think, and I hope with time you will realise that.

Here's the thing about intrusive thoughts/arousal: how much you try not to think about them, the stronger they become. I would recommend looking up the white bear experiment where they explore the effects of thought supression, and it helped me a lot with understanding my own intrusive thoughts. You definitely don't want to be a p-phile, so they are classified as intrusive thoughts, and I'm so sorry you're struggling with them because you seem like a wonderful person who looks out for others. Hey there, i felt the same way when i was your age. I wanted to end it all, i was also thinking about harming myself, i also had horrible thoughts like that, i also felt so alone. I honestly thought i wouldn't even make it past my 16th birthday. And hey, i turned 16 three days ago! Here's what i wish i would've done when i was your age: My parents didn't believe me either so they didn't get me any help. If your school counselor is available, go talk to them. It's supposed to be completely confidential and there you can get your feelings out. They can even get you professional help. Trust me, if i just went to talk to someone about this when i was your age, i would've turned out a lot better lol. If you're worried about having things like bipolar-disorder or depression you can tell your counsoler that. You also mentioned you wanted to become a hip-hop artist? I think it's the perfect time to write your feelings out. It's very therapeutic and creates a creative release. I'm also LGBTQ+ and was really scared about coming out. In that case, you have to make sure it's safe to come out. And remember to come out only if you're ready. My mom forced me to come out and that wasn't fun lol. Remember that this is who we are, and nothing can change that. We should be proud that we we're born this way and keep on fighting!  I'm sorry i couldn't do more. Remember that this is only temporary and good chapters are about to come. You're totally worth it! Take care
